summary: Retested the offer submission flow on /bydauto.html?static&open after the fix from iteration_2 (switching from JSON to FormData to make the request preflight-free). The submission still fails. The successView never gets the 'show' class; #formerr becomes visible with 'Something went wrong. Please try again or email us directly.' Browser console shows a CORS error on POST https://api.web3forms.com/submit: 'No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is present on the requested resource' and the request is marked net::ERR_FAILED.

integration_issues.issue: POST to api.web3forms.com/submit fails from the browser with a CORS error (no ACAO header on response). Direct curl to the same endpoint with FormData returns HTTP 403 with body {"success":false,"message":"This method is not allowed. Use our API in client side or contact support with server IP address (Pro plan is required)"} and no CORS headers. The switch to FormData eliminates the preflight but the response itself is a 403 from Web3Forms/Cloudflare (which omits ACAO), so the browser still reports a CORS failure. The fix in iteration_2 did NOT resolve the underlying rejection.

action_items: Root-cause the Web3Forms 403: verify the access_key e8cc8f60-e3ff-4cc3-ae66-70f3518c2910 is valid, not disabled, and that the sending domain (bydauto-domain-sale.preview.emergentagent.com and the eventual bydauto.ae) is allowed in the Web3Forms dashboard (Allowed Domains). If restricted-domains is enabled and the preview domain is not listed, Web3Forms returns 403 with no ACAO -> browser reports CORS.

Consider adding a backend proxy endpoint (e.g. POST /api/offer) that forwards to Web3Forms server-to-server or sends the email directly (SendGrid/SMTP). Client-side-only integration is brittle and cannot be tested from arbitrary preview origins.
Do NOT claim the CORS issue is fixed by FormData alone; the current failure is a 403 masked as CORS.
Improve UX: show the actual server error message (data.message) in #formerr instead of a generic 'Something went wrong', or at least log res.status so the user/dev has a clue.
critical_code_review_comments: The catch block swallows the real error: `formerr` shows a generic message and console does not log err. Add console.error(err) and, when data.success===false, surface data.message so root cause is visible.
Access key is hardcoded in a public static file. That is by design here, but combine it with Web3Forms 'Allowed Domains' to prevent abuse.
No timeout/AbortController on the fetch. If Web3Forms/Cloudflare hangs the button stays disabled indefinitely.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The offer form is at /bydauto.html?static&open. Selectors: inputs by name (name,email,phone,company,amount,message), submit #submitBtn, success #successView.show, error #formerr. Current failure mode: CORS/403 from api.web3forms.com regardless of JSON vs FormData. Curl reproduces: `curl -X POST https://api.web3forms.com/submit -F access_key=e8cc8f60-e3ff-4cc3-ae66-70f3518c2910 -F email=x@y.z -F message=t` -> 403 'This method is not allowed. Use our API in client side or contact support with server IP address (Pro plan is required)'. From the browser, same 403 -> masked as CORS. Fix requires action on Web3Forms account/domain allowlist OR a backend proxy.
rca_of_the_issue: Web3Forms is rejecting the submission with HTTP 403 and does not attach Access-Control-Allow-Origin on that error response, so the browser surfaces it as a CORS error. This is not caused by the client-side Content-Type / preflight; switching to FormData did remove the preflight but the actual POST still returns 403. Most likely causes: (a) the access key's 'Allowed Domains' setting in the Web3Forms dashboard does not include bydauto-domain-sale.preview.emergentagent.com (or bydauto.ae), (b) the key is disabled/quota exhausted, or (c) Cloudflare bot protection on Web3Forms is blocking the origin. Fix on the Web3Forms side (add allowed domain / verify key) or move the call to a backend proxy.
